claims.claim: A list can be written with comma-separated items between square brackets; lists can contain different types and are sequence types.
Lists support indexing and slicing, and a list slice returns a new list.
List indexes may be negative, while a too-large single index raises IndexError; slice bounds beyond the sequence are handled gracefully.
Lists are mutable: item assignment can replace content and list.append() adds an item at the end.
Simple assignment never copies data: two names can refer to one list, and changes through either name are visible through the other.
A full slice returns a shallow copy of a list; changing a top-level item in that copy does not replace the corresponding top-level item in the original.
